mappings.note: Base numerical: a from (v - u)/t, then F = ma. No friction, graph or reaction pair to add.

Symbolic recall of the second law applied to a combined mass. No value and no model to construct, so LO-6 alone - unlike O36 and N15, where a procedure or an expression is actually built and C8.1 joins it.
The first law restated in the frictionless idealisation. The frictionless premise is given rather than analysed, so LO-63 is not cited (contrast V74, which makes friction's absence the variable).

The assertion is the rest half of the first law (LO-5); the reason to be validated is the subtler claim that rest counts as a constant velocity of zero, which is LO-64's framing. That reason clause is why this is not LO-5 alone as O52 is.
Inverse proportionality between acceleration and mass with no numbers. The diagram only supplies masses symbolically, so no graph code.
The chain being ordered is precisely LO-64's 'a change in velocity is caused by a force', with the second law supplying the acceleration step (LO-6). No magnitudes, so not LO-7.

An experimental procedure for measuring limiting friction with a spring balance. LO-63 carries the quantity being measured; the procedure-design and instrument-reading aspects have no outcome in this frame at all, so no second code is honest here.

Equal forces from the third law (LO-8), unequal accelerations from a = F/m (LO-6). The comparison is qualitative, so LO-6 rather than the LO-7 used for O47, where every row had to be checked numerically.
Scope question on the third law only - does it reach non-contact forces. Duplicate in substance of O40 and mapped identically.
Inverse proportionality again, phrased as a lab manipulation. No value is produced, so LO-6 not LO-7; and nothing is designed or plotted, so the 'experiment' wording does not earn C8.1.

Asks for the momentum form of the second law. LO-6 names the law only 'in terms of mass and acceleration', so momentum has no exact home in this frame - LO-6 is the nearest legal code. Flagged as a poor fit.
Everyday safety device explained by the second law through a longer stopping time - same pair as N8, O14, O21 and V81.
Numbers are given and a value is produced by summing the three masses and dividing, so LO-7. Its symbolic twin O51 takes LO-6 - this is the numeric/symbolic split used throughout the chapter.

The student must sort four everyday events by which law explains each and find the odd one out (swimming, a third-law case). It is a routing question across everyday applications, so LO-65 alone and not either specific law.
Rests on knowing the SI unit of force, LO-7's tail clause; the kilogram half of the analogy is outside this frame. Same partial fit as O19.
Reverses LO-64: zero acceleration implies zero net force. Argued through F = ma but no value is computed, so not LO-7.
Force is defined by its effects - changing the state of motion (LO-64) and changing the direction of motion (LO-61). The 'change of shape' effect again has no outcome in this frame.
SI unit of force including the lower-case name and capital symbol convention - LO-7's define-the-unit clause.

Spring balance as the instrument for the magnitude of a force. The frame has no measurement outcome; LO-7 is cited because measuring a force in newtons is the practical face of its unit clause. Flagged as a weak fit.
Direction alongside magnitude - LO-61 verbatim, in short-answer form (the MCQ twin is O1).
Definition of balanced forces, which is LO-62's definitional core. No motion state is inferred, so not LO-64 - that is the split against V71.

Names the unbalanced case (LO-62) and states the consequence, that the object starts moving in the direction of the larger force (LO-64). V70 has no consequence clause, which is the split between the pair.
The general rule for combining opposing forces, with the direction of the resultant explicitly required (LO-61). Generalised form of O5 and O6.
Friction as the decelerating agent (LO-63) in a familiar event (LO-65). Not LO-64: the question asks for the cause, not for a net-force verdict.

The first law in the frictionless limit (LO-5) with friction's absence as the explicit variable (LO-63). O52 is its MCQ twin but there the premise is merely given, which is why that one carries LO-5 alone.
